**Kenneth Gordon Faulkner** (10 September 1923 – 2000) was an English [footballer] who played in the [Football League] for [Birmingham City].[[3]]

Faulkner was born in [Smethwick], [Staffordshire]. [Capped] "Cap (sport)") by [England at schoolboy level], he had a successful trial with [Birmingham City] during the Second World War.[[4]] Faulkner, a [forward] "Forward (association football)"), played for Birmingham in the [1944–45 season] of wartime competition,[[5]] and also made guest appearances for [Coventry City] and [Port Vale].[[6]] He made his debut in the penultimate game of the 1946–47 [Second Division] season, playing at [outside right] in a 2–0 win at [Millwall]. The last game of that season proved to be his last for the club;[[7]] he was released in the 1947 close season and joined [Oldbury United].[[4]]

In [English football], the **Second City derby**[[1]] or **Birmingham derby** is the [local derby] between the two major clubs in the city of [Birmingham]—[Aston Villa] and [Birmingham City]—first contested in 1879. Villa play at [Villa Park] while Birmingham play at [St Andrew's] "St Andrew's (stadium)"), the two grounds separated by roughly 2.4 miles (3.9 km). It is known as the _Second City Derby_ based on Birmingham being referred to as the [second city of the United Kingdom]. The two clubs are generally regarded as each other's most fierce rivals. In addition both sides have affiliated women's sides, [Aston Villa] and [Birmingham City]. The teams have not met since Villa's promotion to the [Premier League] in 2019.

The clubs first met on [27 September 1879], when Birmingham City were called Small Heath Alliance. The game, on a pitch at Small Heath's [Muntz Street] ground described by the Villa players as "only suitable for pot-holing",[[2]] finished 1–0 – recorded as "one goal and a disputed goal to nil"[[3]] – to the home side.[[4]] Villa won the first competitive game between the clubs, in the Second Round of the [FA Cup] at [Wellington Road] "Wellington Road (Perry Barr)") in 1887, by four goals to nil,[[5]]

The last pre-league FA Cup campaign saw the first competitive "Second City derby" occur on [5 November 1887]. Villa beat Small Heath 4–0 in the fifth round. [Tommy Green] "Tommy Green (footballer, born 1863)") scored a brace before half-time with [Albert Brown] "Albert Brown (footballer, born 1862)") and [Albert Allen] adding to the score in the second half. This was their first meeting with modern rivals [Birmingham City].[[6]]

The first league encounter, in the [First Division] in the [1894–95 season], saw Villa win 2–1.[[7]] after Birmingham had been promoted to the first division for a two year stint.

Small Heath F.C. took part in the [1900–01 FA Cup], losing in the third round to First division Aston Villa after a replay, Villa's Billy Garraty being the sole scorer over the two fixtures. That season Small Heath finished runners-up in [Second Division], so were [promoted] to the [First Division] for [1901–02].[[8]] Villa won 2–0 at [Coventry Road Muntz Street] with goals by [Jack Devey] and [Joe Bache].[[9]] In the 1901 Boxing Day fixture, Villa's [Jasper McLuckie] was the only scorer.[[10]] At the end of the season Birmingham were [relegated] back to the Second Division.

Birmingham were promoted to the First Division in 1903–04 and Second City derbies were played up to 1907–08 when they were relegated. The teams would not meet again in top flight competition until fifteen years later when Birmingham were again promoted to the first division for 1921–22. The derbies continued until [Aston Villa] were relegated [in 1935–36]. The two teams have engaged in several hotly contested matches. In the 1925 league game at [Villa Park], with the home side 3–0 ahead with eleven minutes to go, Blues scored three times in a dramatic final spell to draw the match.[[11]] The following year, Aston Villa made headlines with the signing of [Tom 'Pongo' Waring], and his first appearance was for [the reserves] against Birmingham City's reserves, which famously drew a crowd of 23,000. Waring scored three times in the match.[[12]]

Villa were promoted for the [1938–39 season]. Both teams won their home games.[[13]] Following Birmingham's relegation there would be no further derbies until their promotion for the [1948–49 season].

Ken Faulkner’s senior‑team spell was with **Birmingham City**.  
The only first‑team side that ever beat the 1894‑95 FA Cup winners (Aston Villa) in the modern era was Birmingham City, and the last time that happened was on **16 January 2022** – a 4–1 victory over Aston Villa in the Premier League.
